translations.text: For they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, and like a garden that has no water.
To enter the holes of solid rock and the clefts of the rocks, away from the terror of the Lord and the glory of his might, when he rises to shake the earth.
He will answer on that day and say, “I will not be a ruler, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house, and I will not be a ruler of this people.”
And they say, “Let us bind the righteous man, for he has become disagreeable to us.” From now on they will eat the fruits of their own deeds.
The fine linen, the sky-blue cloth, the red [?], the striped cloth, the gold-striped cloth, and the gold [?].
And your beautiful son, whom you love, will die by the sword, and your rulers will fall by the sword.
And there will be shade from the heat and a sheltering roof against harsh weather and rain.
They will neither hunger nor grow weary; they will neither doze nor sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, nor will the straps of their sandals break.
And in the year in which King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and exalted throne, and the house was full of his glory.
They cried out to one another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”
Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depths or in the heights.
And he says, “Now listen, house of David! Does it seem a small thing to you to weary people? And how is it that you weary the Lord?”
He will eat butter and honey; before he knows or desires evil, he will choose what is good.
And the Lord says to me, “Take for yourself a large new scroll and write on it with the pen of a skilled man: ‘Quickly, quickly take the spoil, and swiftly gather the plunder, for it has arrived.’”

He will be a sanctuary for you, and your foot will not strike a stone, nor will you encounter a stumbling block. But the house of Jacob will be in a snare and in the pits of those lying in ambush in Jerusalem.

For a child was born to us, a son was given to us, whose authority rested on his shoulders, and his name was called Messenger of Great Counsel, Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Ruler, Father of the world to come.
For the word is brief and concise in righteousness; the Lord of hosts will make the word concise throughout the whole world.

Therefore this is what the Lord, the Lord of hosts, says: “Do not fear the Assyrians, my people who dwell in Zion, even if they strike you with a rod; for I bring blows upon you to make you know the way of the Egyptians.”
And the Lord God will raise blows against them like the blows against Midian at the place of torment, and his wrath will be like that along the way through the sea at the departure of the Egyptians.
But he will uphold the rights of the poor and rebuke the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will destroy the ungodly.
And Ephraim’s envy will be removed, and Judah’s enemies will perish. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not envy Ephraim.
And the Lord will destroy the sea of the Egyptians and stretch his hand over the river with a fierce wind. He will strike its seven channels so that it can be crossed confidently, even with shoes on.
And you will say on that day, “I will bless you, Lord, for you were angry with me, but you turned your wrath away from me and had mercy on me.”
Raise a banner on the level mountain; lift your voice against them. Do not be afraid. Beckon with your hand. Open up, rulers, and I will give the command.
Wail, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction from God has arrived.
For the stars of heaven, together with Orion and all the adornment of heaven, will give no light. The sun will be darkened as it rises, and the moon will not give its light.
Look, I am raising up against you the Medes, who consider silver and gold to be nothing.
The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. They will rest in their own land, and the foreigner will join the house of Jacob.
And on that day the Lord will give you rest from your pain, from your anger, and from the harsh slavery in which you served them.
The trees of Lebanon trampled on you, and the cedars of Lebanon say, “Since you ceased, no woodcutters have come up against us.”

Do not rejoice, all you foreigners, because the yoke of those who struck you has been broken. For offspring of vipers will come from the serpent’s descendants, and winged serpents will come from their offspring.
Wail, gates of the cities! Let the cities cry out, all you troubled foreigners! Smoke has risen from the north, and it will no longer be found.
Mourn for yourselves, for Dibon, the site of your temple, has perished. Go up there to weep, to Nebo of the Moabites. Wail, for every head is bald and every arm is broken.
The water of Nimrim will diminish and dry up, its grass will dwindle, and no green plant will be found there. Can he be saved even so?
This is the word that the Lord spoke long ago concerning Moab.
Woe to the multitude of many nations! Like the sea heaped up in waves, so you will rage, and the muscles of many nations will roar like water.
And I saw that the same rider was coming with two horses. He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen and been overthrown, and all its images and its handmade objects have been smashed to the ground.”
Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of Tema; go out with bread to meet the fugitives.
Look, the Lord of hosts will drive you out and destroy you, O man, and will remove your robe and the crown of your glory.
Your hand, with which you used to anger kings, will no longer prevail over the sea. The Lord of hosts has commanded that Canaan’s strength be destroyed.
Wail, ships of the Carthaginians, for your stronghold has perished.
For the earth became lawless through its inhabitants, because they transgressed the Lord’s laws, trampled on his commands, and broke the everlasting covenant.
Wail over the wine everywhere. All joy has fallen silent; all the earth’s joy has been vanquished.
On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judea: “Look, a fortified city! Our salvation will establish walls and ramparts.”
And everyone who does not learn righteousness on earth will not act truthfully. Let the ungodly be taken away, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord.
Lord, your arm is raised high, but they did not recognize it. They will recognize it and be ashamed, and jealousy will seize the undisciplined people. And now fire will devour the adversaries.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to the glorious ones of the earth. You have stretched out to all the ends of the earth.
On that day the Lord will set a barrier from the channel of the River as far as the region of Rhinocorura. But you, gather the children of Israel one by one.
And the flower of hope, shaken loose from glory on the summit of the high mountain, will be like an early-ripe fig that someone sees and wants to swallow before taking it in hand.

For they have gone astray through wine; they went astray because of strong drink. The priest and the prophet became foolish because of strong drink; they were swallowed up by wine; they raved in their drunkenness from strong drink; they went astray, for that itself is foolishness.
For whenever it passes through, it will seize you. Morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night, and there will be fear of calamities.
Does he not first soften its surface and then sow a little black cumin and cumin, and then sow wheat, barley, millet, and spelt within their proper boundaries?
Therefore, this is what the Lord says concerning the house of Jacob, whom he chose from Abraham: Jacob will no longer be ashamed, nor will Israel’s face now turn pale.
Pharaoh’s support will become a shame to you, and those who trust in the Egyptians will suffer disgrace.
Its destruction will be like the breaking of a potter’s earthen vessel, shattered into small pieces, so that no one will find a piece of it with which to take up fire or draw a little water.
Your calves and oxen that work the land will eat straw mixed with barley, winnowed on the threshing floor.
The lawless were driven out of Zion; trembling will seize the ungodly. Now who will tell you that a blazing fire is there, or who will tell you about the eternal dwelling place?

For the name of the Lord is great among you. You will have a place where the rivers and waterways are broad and spacious. You will not travel along that route, nor will your rowed ships go there, for my God is great and will not pass me by.
The mighty will fall with them, along with rams and bulls. The land will be drunk with their blood, and their soil will be filled with their fat.
There the hedgehog brought forth its young, and the earth carefully nourished its young. There stags met one another and saw each other’s faces.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was the chief steward, Shebna, the secretary for official correspondence, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
How can you resist even one of the governors who serve my lord, when you rely on Egypt for its horsemen and horses?
Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of Assyria have insulted me.”
Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: “Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, ‘Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hands of the king of Assyria.’”
While he was worshiping in the temple of his idol Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword. They fled to Armenia, and his son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.
Isaiah said to him, “Now hear the words of the Lord of hosts.”

“Look, days will come when they will take everything that is in your house, and everything your ancestors have gathered up to this day, and carry it to Babylon. They will leave absolutely nothing.” But God said that:
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see the salvation of God, for the Lord has spoken.
The grass withered and the flower fell, but the word of the Lord remains forever.
Look, the Lord God comes with power, and his arm with its own dominion. Look, his reward is with him, and his works are before him.

Who raised up righteousness from the east and called him to follow him? He will bring retribution before the nations and terrify kings. He will turn their swords to dust and drive away their arrows like chaff.
But you, Israel, are my servant, Jacob whom I chose, the offspring of Abraham whom I loved.
But I will raise up the one from the north and the one from the east; they will be called by my name. Princes will come, and you will trample them like potter’s clay that the potter treads.

Who will tell what has been from the beginning, so that we may know, and what happened still earlier, so that we may say, “It is true”? There is no one who speaks beforehand, nor anyone who hears your words.
I am the Lord God; this is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to carved images.
I will say to the north, “Bring them,” and to the south, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from a distant land and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”
who say to Cyrus, “Be wise and carry out all my wishes,” who say to Jerusalem, “Be built,” and I will establish my holy temple.
For the sake of Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen one, I will call you by your name and accept you.
For you are God, and we did not know it, the God of Israel, the Savior.
To whom will you liken me? Look and think it over, you who have gone astray.
Remember the former deeds from ages past, for I am God, and there is no one else besides me.
calling birds from the east and from a distant land for what I planned. I spoke and brought it about; I established it and made it. I brought him and made his paths prosper.
Sit grieving and repentant; enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called the power of kings.
Come to me and hear this: from the beginning I have spoken nothing in secret, nor in a dark place of the earth. When it came into being, I was there. And now the Lord God has sent me, and his Spirit.
For your sons whom you lost will say in your hearing, “This place is too cramped for us. Make room for us so that we may live here.”
The Lord God gives me a trained tongue, so that I may know how to speak a word at the right time. He prepared me morning after morning and gave me an ear to listen.
For the one who justifies me is near. Who is my adversary? Let him come and stand among us. And who is the one who judges me? Let him come near me.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant. Those who walked in darkness and had no light, trust in the name of the Lord and take courage in God.
Listen to me, listen to me, people, and you kings, pay attention to me, for laws will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations.
I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar. The Lord of Hosts is my name.
Shake off your dust, rise and sit down, Jerusalem. Loosen the bond around your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For you will not go out in turmoil or leave in flight, for the Lord himself will go before you, and the God of Israel is the one who gathers you.
Look, my servant will understand; he will be raised up and exalted and greatly glorified.
The Lord did not call you as an abandoned, distressed wife, nor as a wife hated since her youth, but God said.
For you will go out with joy and learn with gladness, for the mountains and hills will leap to welcome you joyfully, and all the trees of the forest will clap with their branches.

I will take them to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be acceptable on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.
The Lord God, who gathers the scattered people of Israel, said, “I will gather crowds to him.”
On the great and high mountain is your bed, and you went up there to offer sacrifices.

Whom did you fear and dread, that you lied to me and did not remember me, did not bring me to mind, and did not keep me in your heart? I saw you and disregarded you. I am the one who has existed from eternity, yet you did not fear me.
And I will not seek vengeance against you forever, nor will I be [?] angry with you, for a spirit will go out from me, and I made every breath.
But the lawless will toss like the sea and find no rest, and its water will perish in trampling and mud.
They will feel the walls like blind people and grope like [?]. They will stumble at midday as though it were the middle of the night, and struggle for breath like people at death’s door.
And they will all move along like bears and like doves. We stood waiting for justice, but there was none, and for salvation, but it withdrew from us.
We acted wickedly and lied to the Lord, and turned back from our God. We spoke injustice and rebelled; we conceived and pondered words of injustice in our hearts.
We pushed justice back, and righteousness withdrew from us, for truth vanished from their roads, and they could not walk along the straight path, and righteousness was taken away from them.
Who are these who have flown like clouds and come to me like doves in flocks with their young?
And the sons of foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will offer themselves to you, for in my anger I struck you, and in my mercy I loved you.
But those who gathered it will eat it and bless the Lord, and those who collected it will drink it in the halls of my holy places.
And he remembered the days of old: “Where are Moses and his people, who brought the shepherd of the flocks up from the earth? Where is the one who put the Holy Spirit in them?”
And now turn from heaven and look from your holy temple and from your glory. Where are your zeal and your power? Where is the abundant mercy of your compassion, with which you used to forgive us?
And there will be no one who calls upon your name, nor anyone who remembers to take refuge in you, for you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
And in the face of all this, do you hold back, Lord, and have you remained silent and humbled us so greatly?
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and gather to celebrate a festival in her, all of you who love her. Be glad and rejoice together, you who sit in mourning for her.
For by the Lord’s fire the whole earth will be judged, and by his sword all flesh. Many will be wounded by the Lord.
